title: $18M Global Programmatic Supply Agreement for PulseBid RTB Exchange with 10ms SLA
executive_summary: MediaHold Group proposes a 3-year $18M exclusive integration with PulseBid Exchange for global programmatic supply across US, EU, and APAC. The deal hinges on ultra-low-latency bidding and seamless multi-region sync to support 12 billion daily auctions during peak Q4 scale.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text: PulseBid Exchange proposes to deliver 12 billion daily bid requests with a guaranteed 8-millisecond p99 bid response time globally, including full multi-region audience sync across US-East, EU-West, and APAC-South. All DSP partners will receive 99.99% bid availability with zero throttling during peak Q4 traffic bursts up to 2.5M QPS. We further commit to real-time user ID sync with 100% cookie match rate across all regions within 5 milliseconds, plus dedicated low-latency fiber routes ensuring sub-10-millisecond hard timeout budget compliance on every auction. Our managed service includes 24/7 proactive fraud filtering blocking 99.8% of IVT with no added latency and no scheduled downtime.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text: The exchange architecture processes up to 8 billion daily bid requests at 1.2M QPS sustained, with measured p99 bid response latency of 18-22 milliseconds intra-region and 45-60 milliseconds cross-region between US-East, EU-West, and APAC-South. Standard maintenance windows occur daily 02:00-02:30 UTC with bid availability SLA of 99.9% excluding maintenance, and adaptive throttling engages above 1.4M QPS to protect bidder stability. User ID sync operates via nightly batch reconciliation with hourly delta updates, achieving 62-68% cookie match rate with average sync latency of 250-400 milliseconds. All auctions enforce a 10-millisecond hard timeout budget after which late bids are discarded, and IVT fraud filtering runs asynchronously post-auction adding 30-50 milliseconds, with synchronous pre-bid filtering available only as a paid add-on adding 6-8 milliseconds per request.

commitments.claim: Guaranteed 8ms p99 global bid response time
commitments.proposal_quote: guaranteed 8-millisecond p99 bid response time globally
commitments.spec_quote: measured p99 bid response latency of 18-22 milliseconds intra-region and 45-60 milliseconds cross-region
commitments.explanation: Proposal guarantees 8ms p99 globally, but spec measures 18-22ms intra-region and 45-60ms cross-region, exceeding the guarantee by 2x-7x and making global compliance physically impossible.

commitments.claim: Real-time user ID sync with 100% cookie match rate in 5ms
commitments.proposal_quote: real-time user ID sync with 100% cookie match rate across all regions within 5 milliseconds
commitments.explanation: Spec provides no support for real-time 5ms sync or 100% match; it only describes nightly batch reconciliation with hourly deltas, 62-68% match rate, and 250-400ms latency, with no real-time capability mentioned.

commitments.claim: Dedicated fiber routes ensuring sub-10ms timeout compliance on every auction
commitments.proposal_quote: dedicated low-latency fiber routes ensuring sub-10-millisecond hard timeout budget compliance on every auction
commitments.spec_quote: All auctions enforce a 10-millisecond hard timeout budget after which late bids are discarded
commitments.explanation: Spec confirms a 10ms timeout exists but frames it as a discard cutoff, not a compliance guarantee; proposal vaguely implies fiber ensures compliance without defining routes, measurement point, or liability for discarded late bids.

commitments.claim: Multi-region coverage across US-East, EU-West, and APAC-South
commitments.proposal_quote: full multi-region audience sync across US-East, EU-West, and APAC-South
commitments.spec_quote: cross-region between US-East, EU-West, and APAC-South
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms operational infrastructure and cross-region connectivity across the exact three regions named in the proposal.
